symptoms: Mosaic mottling, leaf distortion, stunted vines, deformed fruit.
cause: Aphid-transmitted virus; spreads rapidly in warm weather.
management: Rogue and destroy infected plants; control aphid vectors with recommended insecticides.
prevention: Use virus-free seedlings, reflective mulches, and resistant varieties where available.

symptoms: Sunken, circular dark lesions with concentric rings on ripening fruit.
cause: Fungal infection favored by warm, humid conditions and rain splash.
management: Apply recommended fungicides (e.g., Mancozeb/Carbendazim); remove infected fruits promptly.
prevention: Seed treatment, crop rotation, and use of tolerant varieties.

symptoms: White powdery fungal patches on leaf surfaces and stems.
cause: Airborne fungal spores, favored by warm days and cool, humid nights.
management: Sulfur-based or systemic fungicides; neem-based botanical sprays.
prevention: Proper plant spacing for airflow; avoid excess nitrogen; resistant cultivars.

symptoms: Leaf mosaic and curling, vine stunting, malformed pods.
cause: Transmitted by aphid vectors between host plants.
management: Remove infected plants early; manage aphid populations.
prevention: Use certified virus-free seed and tolerant varieties.

symptoms: Dark, sunken spots on fruit and leaves; fruit rot at maturity.
cause: Fungal infection favored by humid conditions and poor orchard sanitation.
management: Timely fungicide sprays and removal of infected/mummified fruit.
prevention: Regular pruning for airflow, orchard sanitation, careful post-harvest handling.

symptoms: Raised, corky lesions with a yellow halo on leaves, twigs and fruit.
cause: Bacterial pathogen spread via wind-driven rain and contaminated tools.
management: Copper-based bactericide sprays; prune and destroy infected material.
prevention: Use disease-free planting material; establish windbreaks.

symptoms: Angular yellow lesions on upper leaf surface; grayish mold beneath.
cause: Oomycete pathogen favored by cool, moist conditions and leaf wetness.
management: Targeted fungicides (e.g., Metalaxyl-based); remove crop debris.
prevention: Resistant varieties; avoid overhead irrigation; ensure field drainage.

symptoms: Bright yellow vein network, leaf yellowing, and reduced fruit yield.
management: Control whitefly populations; uproot and destroy infected plants.
prevention: Tolerant varieties, yellow sticky traps, early-season vector monitoring.

symptoms: Dark brown to black leaf spots surrounded by a yellow halo.
cause: Fungal infection favored by warm, humid weather and dense canopy.
management: Recommended fungicide rotation; remove and destroy infected foliage.
prevention: Adequate plant spacing, field sanitation, and resistant varieties.
